zh: 在嘉应末年时有齐彦槐其人，著有一篇《海运南僧议》，条分缕析断言“一举而众善备”，但地方大吏不愿轻易更张。直到湖南安化的陶文毅公陶澍，由安徽巡抚调江苏，锐意革新，消除盐、漕两事的积弊，齐彦槐的建议，才有一个实验的机会。
en: Towards the end of the Jiaqing reign, a man named Qi Yanhuai wrote an essay setting out the case for shipping the southern grain tax by sea. He examined the matter point by point and declared that a single measure would secure a whole range of benefits. Senior provincial officials, however, were reluctant to change established arrangements. The proposal received a trial only after Tao Shu of Anhua, Hunan—later honoured with the posthumous title Wenyi—was transferred from the governorship of Anhui to that of Jiangsu. Determined to reform the administration, Tao set about eliminating longstanding abuses in both the salt system and grain transport.

zh: 这次实验由陶澍亲自主持，在上海设立“海运总局”，他亲自雇好专门运载关东豆麦的“沙船”一千艘，名为“三不象”的海船几十艘，分两次运米一百五十多万石到天津，结果获得极大的成功，省时省费，米质受损极微。
en: Tao personally supervised the trial. He established a Sea Transport Bureau in Shanghai and hired a thousand flat-bottomed sand junks normally used to carry beans and wheat from the northeast, together with several dozen seagoing vessels of the type known as sanbuxiang, or “unlike any of the three.” In two shipments, they transported more than one and a half million shi of rice to Tianjin. The experiment was an outstanding success: it saved both time and money, and very little of the rice deteriorated.

zh: 承运的船商，运漕而北，回程运豆，一向漕船南下“回空”，海船北上“回空”，现在平白多一笔收入，而且出力的船商，还“赏给顶戴”做了官，真正是皆大欢喜。
en: The shipowners carried grain-tax rice north and beans on the return journey. Previously, canal grain boats had returned south empty, while the coastal vessels had sailed north without cargo. Now an additional source of income had appeared. Shipowners who distinguished themselves were even rewarded with official rank and the right to wear the corresponding hat insignia. Everyone was delighted.

zh: 但是到了第二年，这样的好事竟不再做下去！依然恢复河运。因为，不知道有多少人靠这条运河的漕船来剥削老百姓，他们不愿意革新！
en: Yet the very next year this excellent arrangement was abandoned, and river transport resumed. Countless people depended on the canal grain boats as a means of exploiting the population. They had no desire for reform.

zh: 漕运的弊端与征粮的弊端是不可分的，征粮的权责属于州县，这七品的正印官，特称为“大老爷”，在任两件大事：刑名、钱谷。延请“绍兴师爷”至少亦得两名：“刑名师爷”和“钱谷师爷”。县大老爷的成名发财，都靠这两个人。
en: Abuses in grain transport were inseparable from abuses in grain collection. Responsibility for collecting the tax lay with the departments and counties. A county magistrate, a seventh-rank chief official respectfully called “His Honour,” had two major concerns: criminal justice and revenue. He needed at least two of the professional advisers known as Shaoxing secretaries, one specialising in legal cases and the other in money and grain. His reputation and his fortune depended on these two men.

zh: 钱谷师爷的本事不在算盘上，在于能了解情况，善于应付几种人，第一种是书办，世代相传，每人手里有一本底册，哪家有多少田？该纳粮多少？都记载在这本册子上，为不传之秘。
en: A revenue adviser's chief skill lay not in his use of the abacus but in his grasp of local conditions and his ability to deal with several kinds of people. The first were the clerks, whose positions passed down through their families. Each kept a master register recording how much land each household possessed and how much grain tax it owed. These records were jealously guarded secrets.

zh: 第二种是“特殊人物”，他们所纳的粮，都有专门名称，做过官的绅士人家的“衿米”，举人、秀才、监生是“料米”，这两种米不能多收，该多少就多少，否则便有麻烦。再有一种名为“讼米”，专好无事生非打官司的讼棍所纳的粮，也要当心。总而言这一名话，刁恶霸道，不易对付的那班“特殊人物”，必须敷衍，分量不足，米色粗劣，亦得照收不误。甚至虚给“粮串”——纳粮的凭证，买得个安静二字。
en: The second group consisted of people with special standing. Even the grain they paid had distinctive names. Grain from gentry households whose members had held office was called jinmi; that paid by holders of provincial examination degrees, lower examination qualifications, or Imperial Academy status was called liaomi. Neither group could be made to pay more than its proper assessment without causing trouble. Another category, songmi, was the grain paid by habitual litigants who delighted in stirring up lawsuits. They too had to be handled carefully. In short, the troublesome, overbearing people who were difficult to manage had to be kept satisfied. Their grain had to be accepted even if it was short in weight or poor in quality. Sometimes tax receipts were issued without payment at all, simply to buy peace.

zh: 有人占便宜，当然有人吃亏，各种剥削耗费，加上县大老爷自己的好处，统统都出在良善小民头上，这叫做“浮收”，最“黑”的地方，“浮收”到正额的一半以上，该纳一石米的，起码要纳一石五斗。于是有所谓“包户”，他们或者与官吏有勾结，或者能挟制官吏，小户如托他们“包缴”，比自己到粮柜上去缴纳，便宜得多。
en: If some people gained, others inevitably lost. Every exaction and expense, together with the magistrate's own share of the proceeds, fell on the honest, ordinary taxpayer. This was called “excess collection.” In the worst places, the excess amounted to more than half the official assessment: a household owing one shi of rice had to deliver at least one and a half. Hence the rise of tax contractors. Some colluded with the officials; others could bring pressure to bear on them. For small households, paying through these contractors was much cheaper than delivering their grain directly to the tax office.

zh: 第三种就是漕船上的人。漕船都是官船，额定数字过万，实际仅六千余艘，分驻运河各地，一地称为一帮。这就是游侠组织“青帮”之帮的出典。
en: The third group consisted of the men who worked on the grain boats. These were government vessels, officially numbering more than ten thousand but in reality only a little over six thousand. They were stationed in groups along the canal, each local group being called a bang. This was the origin of the word bang in the name of the Green Gang, the fraternity of men who lived by their own code.

zh: 帮中的管事及水手，都称为帮丁，其中又有屯丁、旗丁、尖丁之分。尖丁是实际上的头目，连护漕的千总、把总都得听他的指挥。州县衙门开仓怔粮，粮户缴纳，漕船开到，验收装船，名为“受兑”。一面征粮，一面受兑，川流不息，那自然是再顺利不过的事，但是这一来漕船上就玩不出花样来了。
en: Both the managers and the sailors in these associations were known collectively as transport servicemen. Among them were men attached to military farming settlements, ordinary registered boatmen, and headmen. The headmen were the real leaders: even the military captains and lieutenants assigned to escort the grain had to follow their instructions. When local offices opened their granaries for tax collection, households delivered their grain, and the transport boats arrived to inspect and load it. This process was called acceptance and transfer. If collection and loading proceeded continuously together, everything could hardly have gone more smoothly. But such efficiency would have left the boatmen no opportunity to play their tricks.

zh: 他们的第一个花样是“看米色”。由于漕船过淮安时，漕运总督要“盘粮”点数，到通州起岸入仓时，仓场侍郎要验看米质，如有不符，都由漕船负责，因此，他们在受兑时，验看米色，原是分所当为。但米色好坏，仅凭目视，并无标准，这样就可以挑剔了，一廒一廒看过去，不是说米色太杂，就是不够干燥，不肯受兑。
en: Their first trick concerned the inspection of the rice. When the boats passed Huai'an, the director-general of grain transport checked the cargo quantities; when the grain was landed and stored at Tongzhou, the granary vice-minister inspected its quality. The boats were responsible for any discrepancy. It was therefore perfectly proper for their crews to examine the rice before accepting it. Quality, however, was judged by sight alone, without an objective standard. That left ample room for fault-finding. The inspectors went from one granary compartment to another, claiming that the rice was too mixed or insufficiently dry, and refused to accept it.

zh: 以一般的情况而言，开仓十日，所有的仓厥就都装满了，此时如不疏运上船，则后来的粮户，无仓可以贮米，势必停征。粮户也就要等待，一天两天还不要紧，老百姓无非发发牢骚而已，日子一久，废时失业，还要贴上盘缠，自然非吵不可，这叫做“闹潜”，是件极严重的事，地方官往往会得到极严厉的处分。倘或是个刮地皮的贪官，这一闹漕就不定就会激起民变，更是件可以送命的大祸。
en: Under normal circumstances, all the granary compartments would be full within ten days of the start of collection. Unless the grain was moved out and loaded onto boats, later arrivals would have nowhere to deposit their rice, and collection would have to stop. The taxpayers would be left waiting. A day or two might bring no more than grumbling, but a longer delay kept them from their work and forced them to spend money on lodging and food. Trouble was inevitable. Such disturbances over the grain tax were a serious matter and often brought severe punishment upon local officials. If the magistrate was especially rapacious, a disturbance might even develop into a popular revolt—a disaster that could cost him his life.

zh: 因此，钱谷师爷，便要指挥书办出来与“看米色”的旗丁讲斤头，倘或讲不下来，而督运的委员，怕误了限期，催令启程，那些帮丁就不问兑足不兑足，只管自己开船。这时的州县可就苦了，必须设法自运漕米，一路赶上去补足，称为“随帮交兑”。
en: The revenue adviser would therefore send the clerks out to bargain with the boatmen responsible for inspecting the rice. If no agreement could be reached and the transport commissioners, anxious about the deadline, ordered the fleet to leave, the crews would sail regardless of whether their full quota had been loaded. That left the local authorities in a miserable position. They had to arrange their own transport, pursue the fleet, and deliver the outstanding grain along the way, a practice known as “following the fleet to complete delivery.”

zh: 幸而取得妥协，漕米兑竣，应该出给名为“通关”的收据，这时尖丁出面了，先议“私费”，就是他个人的“好处”，私费议妥，再议“通帮公费”，是全帮的好处。这些看米色所受的勒索，以及尖丁私费、通帮公费，自然羊毛出在羊身上，由浮收来支付。
en: If a compromise was reached and the grain finally accepted, the crews were supposed to issue a clearance receipt. At this point the headman appeared. First came negotiations over his “private expenses”—his personal reward. Once that had been settled, there were the “public expenses of the whole association,” a payment for everyone's benefit. The money extorted during inspection, the headman's private reward, and the association's collective payment all came, of course, from the same source: the excess grain collected from the taxpayers.

zh: 这以后，就该帮丁受勒索了，首先是“过淮”投文过堂，照例有各种陋规，一帮船总要花到五六百两到一千两银子。这一关一过，沿路过闸过坝，处处要送红包，大概每一艘船要十几两银子。最后到了通州，花样更好，要投四个衙门的文，有人专门代办，每船十三两银子，十两铺排四个衙门，三两是代办者的酬劳。等漕米上岸入仓，伸手要钱的人数不清，总要花到三五十两。所以帮丁勒索州县，无非悖入悖出。
en: After that, it was the boatmen's turn to be extorted. First came the formal submission of documents and appearance before the authorities at Huai'an, accompanied by the customary unofficial fees. A fleet generally had to spend between five or six hundred and a thousand taels to pass this stage. Beyond it, every lock and dam required another payment, adding up to a dozen or more taels per boat. At Tongzhou, the arrangements were still more elaborate. Documents had to be submitted to four government offices. Professional intermediaries handled the process for thirteen taels a boat: ten to distribute among the offices and three for themselves. When the rice was finally landed and stored, so many hands reached out for money that another thirty to fifty taels would be spent. What the boatmen extorted from the counties was, in effect, taken from them in turn.

zh: 帮丁的苦楚犹不止此，一路还要受人的欺侮。在运河里，遇到运铜运铅的船，以及木排，千万要当心，那是在运河是蛮不讲理出了名的，撞沉了漕船，他们可以逃散，帮丁则非倾家荡产来赔不可，因为如此，帮丁便格外团结，以求自保，“青帮”之起因如此，所以，他们的“海底”名为“通漕”，并不是世俗所称的“通草”。
en: Their troubles did not end there. They also suffered intimidation along the route. On the canal, they had to be especially wary of vessels carrying copper or lead and of timber rafts, whose crews were notorious for their lawlessness. If they rammed and sank a grain boat, they could scatter and disappear, while the grain boat's crew might have to sacrifice everything they owned to compensate for the loss. The boatmen consequently formed unusually close bonds for their own protection. This was how the Green Gang began. Its secret code was therefore called Tongcao, meaning “the grain-transport connection,” rather than the similarly pronounced name of the rice-paper plant, as people commonly supposed.

zh: 一度行之有效，但以积习已深，惯于更张的南漕海运，终于咸丰元年旧事重提。这出于两个原因，第一个是人，第二个是地。
en: Sea transport for the southern grain tax had proved effective once, only to be abandoned because entrenched habits resisted change. In the first year of Xianfeng, it was finally proposed again. Two factors brought this about: one concerned a person, the other the physical circumstances.

zh: 这个人是两江总督陆建瀛，湖北人，极能干，而且善于结交，所以公卿延誉，负一时物望。他颇有意步武陶澍，留一番政绩。陶澍改盐法，淮北行之大效，而淮南依旧，陆建瀛在淮南继陶未竟之功。漕运也是如此，他得到户部尚书孙瑞珍的支持，准备恢复海运。
en: The person was Lu Jianying, the governor-general of Liangjiang. A native of Hubei, he was highly capable and skilled at cultivating connections. Senior officials praised him, and he enjoyed considerable public esteem. He wished to follow Tao Shu's example and leave a record of achievement. Tao's salt reforms had worked well north of the Huai River, while the old system remained in place to the south. Lu took up Tao's unfinished work there. He intended to do the same with grain transport and, with the support of Sun Ruizhen, president of the Board of Revenue, prepared to restore sea shipments.

zh: 适逢其会的是，运河出了问题，在徐州附近的丰县以北决口，“全河北趋，由沛县之华山、戚山分注微山、昭阳等湖，挟清水外泛，运河闸、坝、纤堤，均已漫淹”，朝廷一方面拨巨款抢救，一方面也加强了改用海运的决心。
en: At just this moment, disaster struck the canal. A breach opened north of Fengxian, near Xuzhou. “The entire river turned north; from Huashan and Qishan in Peixian it poured into Weishan, Zhaoyang, and the other lakes, driving their waters outward until the canal's locks, dams, and towpath embankments were all submerged.” The court allocated substantial funds for emergency repairs, while its resolve to adopt sea transport grew stronger.

zh: 海运之议，奉旨由两江总督陆建瀛、江苏巡抚杨文定、浙江巡抚常大淳，会同筹划。结果决定咸丰二年江苏的苏州，松江、常州、镇江、太仓等四府一州的溜米，改用海运。浙江则是试办，但其间又有反复，未成定议。
en: The emperor ordered Lu Jianying, Governor Yang Wending of Jiangsu, and Governor Chang Dachun of Zhejiang to draw up a joint plan. They decided that in the second year of Xianfeng the grain from Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang prefectures, together with Taicang department, would travel by sea. Zhejiang was to conduct a trial, but repeated changes of direction there prevented a final decision.

zh: 就在这段期间中，椿寿由湖南布政使调浙江。当朝命初下时，黄宗汉是掌理一省司法的浙江按察使，通称“臬司”，等椿寿到任时，他已经调差了。
en: It was during this period that Chunshou was transferred from the provincial treasury of Hunan to that of Zhejiang. When the appointment was first announced, Huang Zonghan was serving as Zhejiang's provincial judicial commissioner, commonly known as the niesi, responsible for the administration of justice throughout the province. By the time Chunshou arrived, Huang had already been transferred elsewhere.

zh: 第二天，洪军由广西而湖南，湖北吃紧，清文宗把善于“捕盗”的常大淳，调为湖北巡抚。浙江巡抚由藩司椿寿署理。
en: The next day, with Hong's forces moving from Guangxi into Hunan and the situation in Hubei becoming urgent, the Xianfeng emperor transferred Chang Dachun, known for his skill at suppressing bandits, to the governorship of Hubei. Chunshou became acting governor of Zhejiang.

zh: 椿寿的运气太坏。这年的浙江，省城杭州及附近各州县，自五月以后，雨量稀少，旱荒已成，于是对他发生两大不利，第一是钱粮征收不起，第二是河浅不利于舟行，影响漕运。
en: Chunshou's luck could hardly have been worse. From the fifth month onward, little rain fell in Hangzhou or the surrounding districts, and drought had taken hold. This created two serious difficulties for him. Tax revenues could not be collected, and shallow waterways obstructed navigation, delaying the grain shipments.

zh: 江苏的海运，非常顺利，四府一州的漕粮，糙米三十二万多石，白米二万七千余石，于三月间出海北上，安然运到。而浙江的漕米，到九月间还未启运，这是前所未有现象。
en: Jiangsu's sea transport proceeded smoothly. More than 320,000 shi of unpolished rice and over 27,000 shi of polished rice from the four prefectures and one department sailed north in the third month and arrived safely. Zhejiang's grain, however, had still not been dispatched by the ninth month—an unprecedented situation.

zh: 在此以前，也就是渐江正闹旱灾的五月间，为了军事上的需要，各省巡抚有个小小的调整，云南巡抚张亮基调湖南，遗缺由甘肃布政使黄宗汉接充。
en: Earlier, in the fifth month, while Zhejiang was suffering from drought, military needs had prompted a small reshuffle of provincial governors. Zhang Liangji, governor of Yunnan, was transferred to Hunan, and Huang Zonghan, then provincial treasurer of Gansu, was appointed to succeed him.

zh: 他不愿意去云南，经过一番活动，很快地改调浙江。不过一年的功夫，重回杭州时，已非昔比。
en: Huang did not want to go to Yunnan. After some manoeuvring, he soon secured a reassignment to Zhejiang. Barely a year had passed, yet when he returned to Hangzhou, his position was greatly changed.

zh: 署理巡抚椿寿交卸以后，仍旧干他的藩司。据说黄宗汉在第一天接见椿寿时，就作了个暗示，椿寿的“纱帽”在他手里，如果想保全，赶快送四万两银子的“红包”过去。黄宗汉敢于作此勒索，就因为椿寿在漕运上，已经迟延，如果上司肯替他说话。可以在天灾上找理由，有处分，亦属轻微。否则，耽延了“天瘦正供”，将获严谴。
en: After handing over the acting governorship, Chunshou resumed his duties as provincial treasurer. It was said that at their first meeting Huang hinted that Chunshou's official cap—his position—was in Huang's hands. If he wished to keep it, he should promptly send a gift of forty thousand taels. Huang dared make this demand because Chunshou was already behind schedule with the grain shipments. A sympathetic superior could plead the natural disaster on his behalf and keep any penalty light. Otherwise, delaying the grain due to the imperial storehouses could bring severe punishment.

zh: 椿寿没有理会他，于是黄宗汉想了个极狠毒的手法来“整”人。他认为本年漕粮，启运太迟，到达通州交仓，粮船不能依照限期“回空”，这样便要影响下一年的漕运。就在这个言之成理的说法上来整椿寿。
en: Chunshou ignored him, so Huang devised a particularly cruel way to deal with him. This year's grain, he argued, had been dispatched so late that, after delivering it at Tongzhou, the boats could not return empty within the prescribed time. That would delay the following year's shipments. It was upon this plausible argument that he built his attack.

zh: 心里已有成算，表面丝毫不露，把椿寿请到抚院来谈公事，问起清运的情形。
en: With his plan already formed, Huang revealed nothing. He invited Chunshou to the governor's office to discuss business and asked how the grain transport was progressing.

zh: 一提到这上面，椿寿自己先就紧张，“回大人的话，”他说，“今年浙江的漕运，无比如何要担处分了！”
en: The subject immediately made Chunshou uneasy. “Your Excellency,” he replied, “there is no avoiding a penalty over Zhejiang's grain transport this year.”

zh: “谁担处分啊？”黄宗汉故意这样问。
en: “A penalty for whom?” Huang asked deliberately.

zh: “自然是司里。”藩、臬两司向巡抚回话，照例自称“司里”。
en: “For this office, naturally.” When addressing the governor, both the provincial treasurer and the judicial commissioner customarily referred to themselves as “this office.”

zh: “这也不担处分的事。”黄宗汉用这句话先做一个伏笔，却又立即撇开不谈，“贵司倒先说说看，究竟因何迟误？”
en: “It is not simply a question of a penalty.” Having planted this warning, Huang immediately moved on. “First tell me exactly what caused the delay.”

zh: “自然是因为天旱水浅，河道干淤。已经奏报过的。”
en: “The drought, naturally. The water is low and the channels have dried up and silted over. This has already been reported to the throne.”

zh: “天旱是五月以后的事。请问，照定例，本省漕船，每年什么时候开，什么时候‘过淮’，什么时候‘回空’？”
en: “The drought began after the fifth month. Tell me, under the regulations, when should this province's grain boats depart, when should they pass Huai'an, and when should they return empty?”

zh: 一连三问，把椿寿堵得哑口无言。照定例，江西和浙江的漕船，限在二月底以前尽数开行。年深日久，定例有变，但至迟亦不会过四月。现在秋风已起，漕船开行的还不过一半，这该怎么说呢？
en: The three questions in succession left Chunshou speechless. Under the regulations, all grain boats from Jiangxi and Zhejiang were supposed to sail before the end of the second month. Time had modified the practice, but even the latest departures should not extend beyond the fourth month. Now the autumn winds were blowing, and scarcely half the boats had left. How could he explain that?

zh: 他迟迟不答，黄宗汉也不开口，是逼着他非说不可。椿寿无奈，只好这样答道：“大人也在浙江待过，漕帮的积弊，还有什么不明白的？漕丁有种种花样，譬如说陈漕带私货罗……”
en: Chunshou hesitated, and Huang remained silent, forcing him to answer. At last he said, “Your Excellency has served in Zhejiang before. Surely you know the longstanding abuses in the transport associations. The boatmen have all sorts of tricks—for instance, carrying private cargo with the previous season's grain...”

zh: 椿寿的话未完，抚台便一个钉子碰了过来：“天下乌鸦一般黑，各省漕丁都是一样的。”
en: Before he could finish, the governor cut him short. “Crows are black everywhere. The boatmen are the same in every province.”

zh: “今年略微不同，因为奉旨筹议南漕海运，漕帮不免观望，这也是延误的原因之一。”
en: “This year is somewhat different. Since the imperial order to consider shipping the southern grain by sea, the associations have been waiting to see what will happen. That is also one reason for the delay.”

zh: “观望什么？”黄宗汉大声问道，“议办海运是来年新漕之事，跟今年何干？”
en: “Waiting to see what?” Huang demanded loudly. “The proposed sea shipments concern next year's new grain. What have they to do with this year's?”

zh: 振振有词一问，椿寿语塞，既然来年有此改变之议，漕丁自不免有所瞻顾，以致鼓不起劲来，但身为藩司，署理抚院，这些地方正该督催，否则便是失职，所以椿寿无同可解。
en: The forceful question left Chunshou without an answer. Naturally, the prospect of change the following year made the boatmen uncertain and dampened their enthusiasm. But as provincial treasurer and acting governor, he ought precisely to have pressed them to proceed. Otherwise, he had neglected his duty. There was no defence he could offer.

zh: “现在怎么办呢？”黄宗汉又忧形于色地说，“事情总要办通才行啊！”
en: “What are we to do now?” Huang went on, assuming a worried expression. “The business must be carried through somehow.”

zh: “是，是！”椿寿赶紧答道，“司里尽力去催，总在这个把月里，一定可以全数启运。”
en: “Yes, indeed!” Chunshou answered quickly. “This office will press them as hard as possible. Within a month or so, all the boats will certainly be on their way.”

zh: “个把月？”黄宗汉皱着眉说，“说老实话，这上面我还不大弄得清楚。反正本年漕运，自前任常中丞调任以后，都由老兄一手经理。以后该如何办理，等我商量了再说。“
en: “A month or so?” Huang frowned. “To be frank, I am not yet very familiar with this business. In any event, since Governor Chang's transfer, this year's grain transport has been entirely under your management. As for what should be done next, let me consult others before deciding.”

zh: 他这段话有两层用意，第一是说目前还不甚了解漕运的情况，等了解了又当别论，留下翻覆的余地，第二是“一手经理”四个字，指明了全部责任。
en: His words served two purposes. By saying that he did not yet fully understand the situation, he left himself free to take a different position once he had learned more. And by stressing that Chunshou had managed it entirely himself, he placed the whole responsibility on him.

zh: 椿寿原是“上三旗”的公子哥儿，这几年在外面历练了一番。纨袴的积习，固已大减，而人心的险，却无深知，哪里去理会得黄宗汉的深意？还只当抚台语气缓和，事无大碍，所以连声应诺，辞出抚院，赶紧召集手下，商议如何设法把未走的船，能够早日开行，只要一出浙江省境，责任就轻得多了。
en: Chunshou had grown up as a privileged young gentleman of the Upper Three Banners. Several years of provincial service had done much to reduce his idle, aristocratic habits, but he still knew little of the treachery people were capable of. How could he grasp Huang's real meaning? He took the governor's milder tone as a sign that nothing was seriously wrong. Assenting repeatedly, he left the governor's office and hurried to summon his subordinates. They must find a way to get the remaining vessels moving as soon as possible. Once the boats crossed Zhejiang's border, his responsibility would be considerably reduced.

zh: 于是椿寿即刻召集督粮道和其他经办漕运的官员，一面宣达了抚台的意思，一面力竭声嘶地要大家“各秉天良”，务必在最短期间内，设法让漕船全数开出。
en: He immediately assembled the grain intendant and the other officials involved in transport. After conveying the governor's views, he urged them, almost shouting himself hoarse, to act according to their consciences and find a way to dispatch every boat with the least possible delay.

zh: 别处都还好办，麻烦的是湖属八帮，浙江湖川府是东南膏腴之区，额定漕粮三十八万八千余石，关系重大，偏偏这八帮的漕船，一艘都动弹不得。
en: Most places presented manageable difficulties. The real problem lay with the eight associations under Huzhou. Huzhou prefecture occupied some of the richest land in the southeast and had an assessed grain quota of more than 388,000 shi, making it especially important. Yet not one boat belonging to its eight associations could move.

zh: 椿寿看看情势严重，不得不亲自到湖州去督催。
en: Recognising the seriousness of the situation, Chunshou had no choice but to go to Huzhou and supervise matters himself.

zh: 湖州运漕，有朵运河的支流，往东沿太湖南岸，入江苏省境平望的大运河。这种交流不到一百里长，但所经的双林，南浔两镇，为膏腴中的膏腴。
en: Huzhou's grain boats used a branch of the canal running east along the southern shore of Lake Tai to join the Grand Canal at Pingwang in Jiangsu. The branch was less than a hundred li long, but it passed through Shuanglin and Nanxun, two towns that were rich even by the standards of this fertile region.

zh: 南浔的殷富，号称“四狮八象”，海内闻名。听得藩台驾到，照例以捐班道台的身分，尽地主之谊，他们饮食起居的讲究，虽不比盐商、河工的穷奢极侈，但已远非一般宫贵之家可比。
en: The wealth of Nanxun's great families, known collectively as the “Four Lions and Eight Elephants,” was famous throughout the country. On learning that the provincial treasurer was coming, they extended the hospitality expected of local men who had purchased the rank of circuit intendant. Their refinements in food and daily living might not match the extravagant excesses of the salt merchants or river-administration circles, but they far surpassed those of ordinary official and aristocratic households.

zh: 身处名匠经营的园林，坐对水陆并陈的盛馔，开宴照例开戏，南浔富家都有自己的戏班，砌末、行头，无不精美，这时集合精英，奏演名曲，而椿寿索然寡欢，却又不得不勉强敷衍，因而这样豪华享受的场台，在他反觉得受罪，耳中听着《长生殴》的《夜雨闻铃》，心里想的却是怎得下他三天三夜的大雨，运河水满，让搁浅的漕船，得以趁一帆西风，往东而去？
en: Chunshou found himself in gardens designed by master craftsmen, seated before sumptuous dishes drawn from land and water. As was customary, the banquet began with an opera performance. Nanxun's wealthy families maintained their own troupes, with exquisite props and costumes. Now their finest performers were brought together to present celebrated scenes. Yet Chunshou took no pleasure in any of it and had to force himself to be polite. What should have been a luxurious entertainment felt instead like an ordeal. As he listened to “Hearing Bells in the Night Rain” from The Palace of Eternal Life, he could think only of how welcome three days and nights of heavy rain would be. If the canal filled, the stranded grain boats could catch a west wind and sail eastward.

zh: 想着漕船，椿寿无论如何坐不住了。托词“身子不爽”，向主人再三道歉告辞，回到行辕。
en: The thought of the boats made it impossible for him to remain seated. Pleading indisposition, he repeatedly apologised to his hosts and returned to his temporary headquarters.

zh: 行辕里已经有许多人在等着。这些人分为三类，一类是漕帮中的“领运千总”，名义上算是押运的武官，照原来的传统，多由武举人中选拔，一类是临时委派的押运官，大多为候补州县，走路子钻上这个差使，多少弄几文“调剂调剂”，再一类就是各帮中真正的头脑：“尖丁”。
en: Many people were already waiting there. They fell into three groups. First were the captains charged with leading the grain convoys, military officers traditionally selected from men who had passed the provincial military examination. Second were the temporarily appointed escort officials, mostly expectant local magistrates who had used their connections to secure an assignment that might bring them a little money to ease their circumstances. Third were the real leaders of the associations: the headmen.

zh: “尖丁”的身分是小兵，这还是明朝“卫所”演变下来的制度。小兵与二品大员的藩台，身分相差不知几许？照平日来说，连见椿寿的面都难，但此刻也顾不得这些官派了！要设法能让漕船开动，非找尖丁来谈，才商议得出切实的办法，所以椿寿吩咐，一体传见。
en: In official status, a headman was merely a common soldier, a survival of the military settlement system of the Ming dynasty. The gulf between such a man and a provincial treasurer of the second rank was immense. Ordinarily, he would scarcely have been allowed into Chunshou's presence. Now, however, official dignity had to yield. Any practical plan for moving the boats required the headmen's participation, so Chunshou ordered that everyone be admitted.

zh: 行辕借在一家富户的两进屋子，时已入夜，轩敞的大厅上，点起明晃晃的火油灯，照出椿寿的满面愁容！他居中坐在红木炕床上，两旁梨花木的“太师椅”上，坐的是候补州县身分的押运官，千总和尖丁便只有站的份儿了。
en: His temporary headquarters occupied a wealthy family's house with two successive courtyards. Night had fallen. Bright oil lamps lit the spacious hall and illuminated the worry on Chunshou's face. He sat in the centre on a mahogany couch. The escort officials awaiting local appointments occupied the pearwood armchairs on either side; the military captains and headmen had to stand.

zh: 在鸦雀无声的沉重的气氛中，椿寿扯开嘶哑的嗓子说道：“今年的漕粮，到底还运得出去，运不出去？”
en: In the heavy silence, Chunshou raised his hoarse voice. “Are we going to get this year's grain shipped or not?”

zh: 这一同大家面面相觑，都要看一看对方的脸色。最有资格答话的是尖丁，但以身分关系，还轮不到他们开口。
en: They looked at one another, each trying to read the others' expressions. The headmen were best qualified to answer, but their low status gave them no right to speak first.

zh: “我在抚台面前，拍了胸脯的，一个月当中，一定全数开船。现在看了实在情形，我觉得我的话说得过分了。今天一定先要定个宗旨出来，船能动是动的办法，不能动是不能动的办法。这样子一天一天等下去，非把脑袋等掉了不可。”
en: “I gave the governor my word that every boat would leave within a month. Now that I've seen the actual conditions, I fear I promised too much. Today we must decide on a course of action. If the boats can move, we need one plan; if they cannot, we need another. If we go on waiting day after day, we'll wait until we lose our heads.”

zh: 这是提出了要砍脑袋的警告，在座的人，无不悚然！坐在左首太师椅上的一名候补州县，便欠身说道：“总得仰仗大人主持全局，属下便赔上性命，也得把漕船开出去。漕粮关乎国家正用，今年天旱水浅，纵然耽迟，还有可说，倘或不走，那就是耽错了。”
en: The warning that heads might fall sent a shiver through everyone present. One of the expectant magistrates in the armchairs on the left leaned forward. “We must rely on Your Excellency to direct the whole affair. Even at the cost of our lives, we must get the grain boats moving. This grain is essential to the state's regular needs. With this year's drought and shallow water, delay may still be excused. But if the boats do not leave at all, that will be failure.”

zh: “耽迟不耽错”这一说，凡是坐在大师椅上的，无不齐声附和。这些候补州县，没有一个不闹穷，有些在省城住了十几年，始终没有补上一个缺，穷得只剩下一叠当票，好不容易才派上这一个押运的差使，指望着漕船一动，便好先支一笔公费安家。至于这一去什么时候才能到达通州，他们不必担心，迟延的处分，落不到他们头上。
en: Everyone seated in an armchair promptly endorsed this distinction between delay and failure. These expectant magistrates were all short of money. Some had lived in the provincial capital for more than ten years without obtaining a substantive appointment, until their possessions had dwindled to a stack of pawn tickets. At last they had secured escort duties. Once the boats moved, they hoped to draw an advance on official expenses to provide for their families. They had no need to worry about when the fleet would reach Tongzhou: any punishment for delay would fall on someone else.

zh: 倘说漕船不走，他们便回不得省城，因为船不走，便无所谓押运，不仅万事全休，而且比不得这个差使还要坏——不得这个差使，不必借了盘缠来到差。现在两手空空回杭州，债主那里如何交代？
en: If the boats did not sail, however, they could hardly return to the provincial capital. No sailing meant no escort duty. They would not merely lose everything they had hoped for; they would be worse off than if they had never received the assignment. Without it, they would not have borrowed money to travel to their posts. How could they return to Hangzhou empty-handed and face their creditors?

zh: 椿寿当然明白他们的用心，而且也知道这些人无足轻重，既出不了什么力，也担不了什么责任，所以不理他们的话，望着站在他们身后的“领运千总”说：“他们有什么主意，说出来商量。”
en: Chunshou understood their motives. He also knew that they carried little weight: they could neither contribute much nor assume any real responsibility. Ignoring their remarks, he looked towards the convoy captains standing behind them. “Tell us what ideas you have, so that we can discuss them.”

zh: “领运千总”的想法，与那些候补州县差不多，只是他们不能胡乱作主，凡事要听尖丁的招呼，因而有个年纪大些的便这样回答：“请大人作主！”
en: The captains thought much as the expectant magistrates did, but they could not make decisions on their own. In everything they had to follow the headmen's lead. One of the older captains therefore answered, “We ask Your Excellency to decide.”

zh: “如果我说不走呢？”
en: “And if I say the boats are not to go?”

zh: 大家都不响，没有一个人赞成他的主意，只是不敢驳回。但这样不作声，也就很明显地表示出反对的意思了。
en: No one spoke. None agreed with the suggestion, but none dared oppose it. Their silence, however, made their opposition plain enough.

zh: 在座的一个实缺同知，此时忍不住开口：“跟大人回话，还是让他们推出一两个人来，看看有何话说？”
en: A substantive deputy prefect present could no longer hold back. “Your Excellency, perhaps they should choose one or two representatives and let us hear what they have to say.”

zh: “他们”是指尖丁，椿寿点点头，对那些尖丁说：“我看也非你们有句话不可。”
en: By “they,” he meant the headmen. Chunshou nodded and turned to them. “I think we must hear from you after all.”

zh: “是！”有个“有头有脸”的尖丁答应一声，请个安说：“请大人先休息。我们商量出一个宗旨，再跟大人回禀。”
en: “Yes, Your Excellency!” replied one of the more prominent headmen, making a respectful salute. “Please rest a little while we confer. Once we have agreed on a proposal, we will report to you.”

zh: “好，好，你们商量。”
en: “Very well. Go and discuss it.”

zh: 椿寿坐在炕床上咕噜噜吸水烟，八帮的尖丁便退到廊下去悄悄商议，好久尚无结论，因为各帮的情况不同，看法各异，牵涉的因素很多。今年的漕运，吃力不讨好是公认的看法，但走与不走，却有相反的主张，一派认为赔累已不可免，不加不走，还省些事，一派则以在漕船上带着许多私货，不走则还要赔一笔，“公私交困”，简直要倾家荡产了。
en: Chunshou sat drawing on his water pipe, which gurgled softly, while the headmen of the eight associations withdrew to the corridor to confer in low voices. A long time passed without agreement. Conditions differed from one association to another, opinions varied, and many interests were involved. Everyone agreed that this year's transport would mean hard work with little reward, but they disagreed over whether to sail. One faction argued that losses were inevitable, so they might as well stay and spare themselves the trouble. The other pointed out that the boats carried substantial private cargoes. Failing to sail would bring losses on those goods too. Caught between public obligations and private business, they could be ruined.

zh: 谈来谈会，莫衷一是，椿寿已经派人来催了，只好听凭上面云决定走与不走。不过总算也有了一点协议“那就是走也好，不走也好，各帮的赔累，只能一次，不能两次。
en: They argued back and forth without reaching a common view. When Chunshou sent someone to hurry them, they could only leave the decision to their superiors. They had, however, agreed on one point: whether the boats sailed or not, the associations could bear one round of losses, but not two.

zh: “如果不走，本年的漕粮便要变价缴纳，户部定章是每石二两银子，现在市价多少？”椿寿问。
en: “If the boats do not sail, this year's grain must be sold and the proceeds remitted,” Chunshou said. “The Board of Revenue fixes the rate at two taels per shi. What is the current market price?”

zh: “这要看米的成色。”被推定去回话的那个尖丁答道：“总在七钱到八钱这个数目之间。”
en: “That depends on the quality,” answered the headman chosen to speak for them. “Somewhere between seven and eight tenths of a tael.”

zh: “船上的漕粮有多少？”
en: “How much grain is on the boats?”

zh: “一共二十七万六千石。”
en: “A total of 276,000 shi.”

zh: “那么，”椿寿问道，“就算每石赔一两二钱银子，共该多少？”
en: “Then,” Chunshou asked, “if we lose one tael and two tenths on every shi, what does that come to?”

zh: 那尖丁的心算极快，略略迟疑了一下，便报出确数：“共该三十三万一千二百两银子。”
en: The headman was quick at mental arithmetic. After scarcely a pause, he supplied the exact figure. “331,200 taels.”

zh: “如果漕船不走，奏请变价缴银，上头一定会准的。不过，”椿寿面色凝重地问，“这三十三万两银子，该谁来赔？”
en: “If the boats cannot sail, the throne will certainly approve a request to sell the grain and remit silver instead. But”—Chunshou's face grew grave—“who is to make up those three hundred and thirty-odd thousand taels?”

zh: “大人晓得的，湖属八帮是‘疲帮’，力量实在够不上。总要请大人格外体恤，留漕丁一条命。”
en: “Your Excellency knows that the eight Huzhou associations are financially exhausted. We simply haven't the means. We must beg you to show special consideration and leave the boatmen a chance to survive.”

zh: “哼！”椿寿冷笑，“你们要命，难道我的命就可以不要？”
en: “Hmph!” Chunshou gave a cold laugh. “You want to save your lives. Is mine the only one that does not matter?”

zh: 这是双方讨价还价，有意做作。漕帮有“屯田”，有“公费”，遇到这种情形，便得从公众的产业和收入中，提出款子来赔，赔累的成数，并无定章，但以上压下，首先要看帮的好坏，公产多的“旺帮”便赔得多，负债累累的“疲帮”便赔得少。说也奇怪，越是富庶的地区，漕帮越疲，第一疲帮是江苏松江府属各帮，溯州府属八帮的境况也不见得好，这因为是越富庶的地区，剥削越多的缘故。
en: Both sides were bargaining, putting on a show. The transport associations possessed agricultural estates and collective funds. In circumstances like these, they had to draw on their common property and income to cover losses. There was no fixed rule governing their share. Pressure came from above, and the first consideration was an association's financial condition. Prosperous associations with substantial communal assets paid more; exhausted associations burdened with debt paid less. Curiously enough, the richer the district, the poorer its transport associations tended to be. Those under Songjiang in Jiangsu were the most impoverished, and the eight Huzhou associations were not much better off. The explanation was that richer districts suffered heavier exactions.

zh: 这赔累的差额，除了漕帮以外，主要的使得由藩司从征收漕粮的各种陋规和“浮收”中，提成分赔。所以处理这件棘手的案子，实际上只是藩台衙门和湖属八帮间的事。椿寿软哄硬逼，总算把分赔的成数谈好了。
en: Beyond the associations' contribution, most of the shortfall had to be met by the provincial treasurer out of a share of the unofficial fees and excess collections associated with the grain tax. In practice, therefore, this difficult affair concerned only the provincial treasury and Huzhou's eight associations. By alternately coaxing and pressuring them, Chunshou finally secured agreement on how the loss would be divided.

zh: 然而这也不过是万不得已的退路。眼光总是朝前看的，能够把漕船开出去，交了差，也免了赔累，何乐不为？所以椿寿又回过头来问：“照你们看，漕船到底能不能动呢？能动还是照开的好。”
en: That, however, was merely a last resort. It was still better to look for a way forward. If the boats could sail, the obligation would be fulfilled and the loss avoided. Why not try? Chunshou therefore returned to the original question. “In your judgement, can the boats move at all? If they can, it would still be better to send them.”

zh: 这一句话自然大受欢迎，在座的候补州县，一看事有转机，无不精神夏振，纷纷颂赞椿寿的明智。
en: The suggestion was warmly welcomed. Seeing a turn for the better, the expectant magistrates brightened at once and competed in praising Chunshou's wisdom.
